name: SSH Brute Force Detection
description: Detection and analysis of repeated SSH authentication failures that may indicate brute force, password spraying, or automated credential guessing.
objective: Identify repeated SSH authentication failures from the same source
Determine whether the activity is low-risk scanning, suspicious brute force, or malicious compromise attempt
analysis_steps: Check the number of failed SSH authentication attempts and the time window
Identify the source IP, destination host, destination port, and targeted user account
Check whether the targeted account is privileged, such as root or an administrator account
Check whether multiple accounts or multiple hosts are targeted
Search for any successful SSH authentication after the failed attempts
Review enrichment results for the source IP when Cortex or MISP reports are available
Determine whether the behavior looks like opportunistic Internet scanning, suspicious brute force, or a confirmed compromise attempt
If enrichment is missing, do not assume that the source IP is malicious

low_risk: No successful authentication after the failures
suspicious: Repeated failed SSH attempts in a short time window
Same source IP is recurrent or targets multiple users
malicious: High-volume or clearly automated brute force behavior
Successful SSH login after repeated failures
Source IP is confirmed malicious by enrichment
Administrative account is targeted or compromised

low_risk: Document the activity as low-risk scanning
Close the alert if no recurrence is observed
suspicious: Keep the alert open for SOC investigation
Review SSH authentication logs over the last 24 to 48 hours
Check for successful login events from the same source IP
Enrich the source IP with available Cortex or MISP sources
Monitor the targeted account and host for recurrence
malicious: Block the source IP at firewall, WAF, or security group level
Reset or disable the targeted account if compromise is suspected
Restrict SSH access to authorized sources
Review command history, active sessions, and persistence indicators on the host
Escalate to SOC or Incident Response for full investigation
